result: In 158 ME/CFS patients vs 67 controls, patients were worse on all main CPT3 measures (inattentiveness, sustained attention, vigilance, impulsivity, slow reaction time), with hit reaction time and its variability the most discriminative.
reason: Independent cohort, same domains (attention, reaction time and its variability), same direction.

result: Muscle biopsies from 11 post-COVID patients with PEM showed fewer capillaries, thicker capillary basement membranes and more CD169+ macrophages than two historical control cohorts, with no SARS-CoV-2 RNA and distinct immune/metabolic transcriptomic signatures.
reason: Resting biopsies on capillarisation and basement membrane, not post-exercise mitochondrial enzymes or necrosis; likely the unpublished basement-membrane source, so check whether already cited.

result: National Norwegian survey of 491 severe (444) or very severe (47) patients: childhood onset in 45% of very severe and 32% of severe, and 71% of very severe patients needed more than 40 h/week of family care; care often inadequate and sometimes harmful.
reason: Self-selected survey of severe patients; it measures neither the prevalence of severe illness nor severity as a predictor of treatment response.

result: Levels of 11 circulating miRNAs differed between ME/CFS, fibromyalgia and comorbid ME/CFS+FM and correlated with symptom severity, and a machine-learning model based on them discriminated the groups (sample sizes and accuracy not given in the abstract).
reason: Omics domain: circulating (not EV) miRNA panel to tell ME/CFS from FM is not covered; small single-lab study without reported numbers.

result: In women given an exercise challenge, ME/CFS patients showed no significant gene-expression changes at peak exertion, whereas controls altered immune signalling networks; in recovery, patients showed dysregulated immune signalling and stress-response pathways.
reason: Post-exercise blood transcriptomics with a different method (genome-wide, not the targeted receptor panel) and a different pattern, so not a replication.

result: Two-sample Mendelian randomisation found no causal effect of genetic liability to COVID-19 susceptibility, hospitalisation or severity on ME/CFS (OR 1.000 for each; p=0.333, 0.862, 0.998).
reason: Tests the same causal claim and finds none, but genetic instruments for infection are weak and the method is not comparable to cohort incidence, so it carries little weight.

result: In 6 women with mild COVID and autonomic testing before and/or after infection, all had sudomotor dysfunction, which was new or worse after infection; parasympathetic function was unchanged, and postural tachycardia occurred in half (new-onset in 1/3).
reason: Objective autonomic testing in long COVID, adding a pre-infection baseline and a sudomotor focus; tiny case series, not an independent replication.

result: Of 13 selected ME/CFS patients (from 101 with 3 or more 10-min stand tests) who passed and failed standing on different occasions, 12 (92%) showed chronotropic incompetence during orthostasis, failing without POTS, and 5 (38%) failed only without POTS.
reason: Does not estimate POTS prevalence; extends chronotropic incompetence from exercise to orthostasis in a small, selected sample.

result: Serum S100beta was higher after acute infection in patients with neurological impairment (n=76), and DCE-MRI in 32 long COVID patients showed raised BBB permeability in frontal, occipital and temporal regions, tracking brain volume loss and TGF-beta.
reason: already cited: preprint of Greene 2024 Nat Neurosci (same cohorts and methods).

result: Isolated NK, CD4+ and CD8+ T cells from ME/CFS patients (n=8-20 per experiment) used more lipids and had higher fatty-acid-oxidation proteins, especially after overnight stimulation, across memory, effector and naive T-cell subsets.
reason: Adds fatty-acid-oxidation dependence to the immune-cell bioenergetics finding (Hanson lab, small n).
